Bradley Sutton finds out in this episode of the Serious Sellers Podcast, recorded at an AI mastermind outside Paris. Through conversations with Carrie Miller, Jared Mortensen, Antonio Bindi, and Cara Sayer, he explores how sellers are using AI today and the systems they are preparing to build next. From organic content to shared company knowledge, the discussions reveal practical opportunities to reduce repetitive work and support growth. Carrie shares her plan to create AI avatars based on customer personas, build audiences on Facebook and Instagram, and direct interested shoppers to Amazon. She also explains how Helium 10 MCP helped her investigate declining advertising sales and identify profitable campaigns that had been switched off. Jared brings a different perspective: his team has already experimented with AI avatars, but manual checks and troubleshooting have limited their efficiency. He discusses testing more hooks, repurposing content across platforms, and developing affiliate partnerships that use creators’ likenesses while continuing to compensate them. items.excerpt: Amazon insiders explain faster shipping, simpler inventory placement, and new AI workflows, plus how Seller Assistant, Canvas, and a Claude plugin could change how sellers grow their brands.
items.body: Amazon insiders explain faster shipping, simpler inventory placement, and new AI workflows, plus how Seller Assistant, Canvas, and a Claude plugin could change how sellers grow their brands. ► Watch The Podcasts On YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@Helium10?sub_confirmation=1 ► Instagram: instagram.com/serioussellerspodcast ► Free Amazon Seller Chrome Extension: https://h10.me/extension ► Sign Up For Helium 10: https://h10.me/signup (Use SSP10 To Save 10% For Life) ► Learn How To Sell on Amazon: https://h10.me/ft What would faster inventory replenishment and an AI assistant that handles tasks mean for your Amazon business? Recorded at Amazon Accelerate in Seattle, this episode brings together Amazon Global Logistics leaders Alex Berry and Heather Hunt, followed by Chris Jones from the Seller Assistant team. Bradley Sutton explores how Amazon is simplifying the work behind selling, from moving products across borders to managing everyday business decisions. Alex and Heather explain how AGL reduced end-to-end transit times from China to the U.S. West Coast by about 20% year over year. They also discuss a premium ocean service that cuts China-to-Europe and UK transit times by approximately 11 days compared with standard service. Amazon Managed Placement at Origin simplifies inventory distribution through one booking, while storage at origin can help sellers replenish inventory based on demand. Other announcements include Ship to 3P for deliveries to non-Amazon warehouses, broader support for dangerous goods, and standalone customs brokerage through Amazon Customs and Trade. Online document management and direct access to logistics operators also aim to reduce paperwork and make shipping problems easier to resolve.
